mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a Mercedes G Class 250/300 Diesel engine in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mercedes G Class 250/300 Diesel engine replacement typically costs between £3,200 and £6,500 depending on engine code, condition type, and whether fitting is included. OM602 units start around £3,200, while OM606 turbodiesel units range from £4,500 to £6,500. Rebuilt OM603 (G 300 GD): £3,500-£5,500 supply only. Rebuilt OM606 (G 300 Turbodiesel): £4,500-£6,500 supply only. Used engines from breakers: £1,200-£4,000 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of OM603 injection pump failure in a G 300 GD?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM603's mechanical Bosch injection pump typically shows warning signs before complete failure - poor cold starting, white smoke on start-up, rough idle, and loss of power are the most common symptoms. Hard starting when cold that improves as the engine warms. White or grey smoke from the exhaust, especially at idle. Injector pump seal leaks (diesel weeping from the pump body). If the pump fails completely, the engine will not start at all.

mainEntity.name: Is the OM606 engine in the G 300 Turbodiesel reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM606 is one of Mercedes' most over-engineered diesel engines and is legendary for longevity - many examples exceed 300,000 miles with basic maintenance. The timing chain is the main weak point, stretching approximately 1 degree per 100,000 miles. Regular oil changes (every 6,000-8,000 miles) are critical for chain life. Timing chain inspection at 150,000 miles is recommended. The engine responds well to specialist tuning (250-300hp achievable). With preventative maintenance, 300,000+ miles is realistic.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my G Class 250/300 Diesel engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., injection pump seals on OM603, timing chain tensioner on OM606, vacuum pump on OM602). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or multiple major failures. OM603 injection pump calibration: £600-£1,000 - excellent value if caught early. OM606 timing chain replacement: £1,200-£1,800 - do this preventatively. Full OM603 rebuild: £3,500-£5,500 - for catastrophic failure or 180k+ miles. Full OM606 rebuild: £4,500-£6,500 - still less than finding a replacement vehicle.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my G Class 250/300 Diesel has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix (e.g., OM602, OM603, OM606). V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block (visible from under vehicle, left side). G 250 GD: OM602.931 (2.5L five-cylinder). G 300 GD: OM603.931 (3.0L six-cylinder naturally aspirated). G 300 Turbodiesel: OM606.964 (3.0L six-cylinder turbocharged).

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used G Class 250/300 Diesel engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a G Class diesel. The complex 4MATIC/4WD system, gearbox alignment, and injection pump timing requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. 4MATIC transfer case alignment requires specialist knowledge. Injection pump timing requires precise calibration tools (OM603/OM606). Engine and gearbox must be separated correctly to avoid damaging the torque converter. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,500 - worth every penny for these classics.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a reconditioned G Class 250/300 Diesel engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty, with many specialists offering 24-month coverage on OM606 rebuilds. This includes parts and labour for any manufacturing defect or installation error. 12-month unlimited mileage is the minimum standard. OM606 rebuilds often include 24-month warranty due to their robust design. All warranties cover parts, labour, and MOT compliance. Extended warranties available at point of purchase.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz G Class 250/300 Diesel - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes Benz G Class 250/300 Diesel encompasses the naturally aspirated and turbocharged diesel variants that defined the G-Class's legendary off-road reputation throughout the W460 and W463 generations - from the 2.5-litre OM602 five-cylinder through to the 3.0-litre OM606 six-cylinder turbodiesel.

milestones.description: OM617 five-cylinder diesel (G 300 GD W460), 88hp, naturally aspirated, the original military-spec diesel
OM602.931 2.5-litre five-cylinder diesel (G 250 GD W460/W463), 92-94hp, the more economical entry-point diesel
OM603.931 3.0-litre inline-six diesel (G 300 GD W463), 113hp, naturally aspirated, replaced the OM617
OM606.964 3.0-litre inline-six turbodiesel (G 300 Turbodiesel W463), 177hp, the high-performance diesel that transformed G-Class capability

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every diesel engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz G Class 250/300 Diesel range is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points from real owner experience.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz G Class 250/300 Diesel Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Benz G Class 250/300 Diesel range relies on three engine families - OM602, OM603 and OM606 - each with well-documented weaknesses. The OM603 dominates classic G-Class diesel replacement demand with injection pump and timing chain issues, while the OM606 offers greater power but shares similar timing chain concerns. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common G Class 250/300 Diesel engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.group: OM603 Injection Pump & Timing Chain Wear
problems.h4: OM603 Injection Pump & Timing Chain Wear - Why the G 300 GD Loses Power and Starts Poorly
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 300 GD (OM603.931, 1990-1993)
problems.rootCause: The duplex timing chain stretches over time, while the mechanical Bosch inline injection pump suffers internal seal wear and calibration drift - both lead to poor starting, excessive smoke, and eventual engine damage.

repairOptions.dealerPrice: Not available (dealers rarely touch classic diesels)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove pump, fit new seals, bench calibrate to factory spec
repairOptions.longevity: 50k-70k miles; for running issues without chain noise

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides; inspect sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles; corrects the root cause properly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM603 with new chain, rebuilt pump, upgraded tensioner
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; required if chain has jumped or pump damage is severe

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G 300 GD in good condition is worth £15,000-£40,000 depending on mileage and condition - the full replacement cost of £3,500-£5,500 is small relative to vehicle value, making a specialist rebuilt engine excellent value for preservation. If the vehicle is worth under £8,000 (high-mileage or project condition), evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: On a classic G 300 GD, we recommend timing chain replacement and pump calibration together as a preventative investment - doing one without the other often leaves the owner chasing problems within 12-18 months. Main dealers are rarely interested in these classics; use a specialist who knows OM60x engines intimately.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM603 Mercedes Benz G Class 250/300 Diesel engine prices

problems.h4: OM606 Timing Chain Stretch - Why the G 300 Turbodiesel Rattles on Start-Up
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 300 Turbodiesel (OM606.964, 1996-2000)
problems.rootCause: The single-row timing chain stretches gradually over time, causing the engine's timing to become inaccurate. While some OM606 examples exceed 300,000 miles on the original chain, stretch of 1 degree per 100,000 miles is typical - eventually leading to rattling on startup and, in worst cases, chain skip with catastrophic valve-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspect chain stretch, replace tensioner only if minimal wear
repairOptions.longevity: 30k-40k miles; only viable if no significant chain stretch

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, all tensioners, guides and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles; corrects the root cause properly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM606 with new chain, tensioner and upgraded guides
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; required if chain has jumped

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G 300 Turbodiesel in good condition is worth £15,000-£35,000 - the full replacement cost of £4,500-£6,500 is modest relative to vehicle value, making a specialist rebuilt engine a sound investment. For vehicles worth under £8,000, evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: At the first sign of cold-start rattle, have the chain stretch measured. If stretch is minimal, the tensioner-only fix (£200-£400) offers good value. If the rattle lasts more than 2 seconds or you've ignored it for 10k+ miles, go straight to the full chain set - the OM606's DOHC design means chain failure is catastrophic and expensive.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM606 Mercedes Benz G Class 250/300 Diesel engine prices

problems.group: OM602 Head Gasket & Vacuum Pump Failure
problems.h4: OM602 Head Gasket & Vacuum Pump Failure - Why the G 250 GD Loses Compression
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 250 GD (OM602.931, 1988-1992)
problems.rootCause: The OM602 five-cylinder diesel is robust but prone to head gasket leaks on high-mileage units, while the vacuum pump's internal bearings can fail without warning - sending debris through the engine and causing catastrophic damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace vacuum pump with updated unit, check for debris
Replace head gasket, pressure test head, new bolts
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles; for compression loss or coolant contamination

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM602 with new head gasket, vacuum pump and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; required if debris damage has occurred

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G 250 GD is worth £10,000-£25,000 depending on condition - the full replacement cost of £3,200-£4,800 is reasonable relative to vehicle value. For vehicles worth under £6,000, a used engine may be more appropriate.
problems.recommendation: The vacuum pump is the OM602's Achilles heel - replace it preventatively at 200,000 miles regardless of symptoms. If the pump fails internally, debris can destroy the engine within minutes. For head gasket issues, specialist replacement at £1,000-£1,600 is excellent value compared to the cost of a full rebuild.
